summary: No exploitable issues in the task-02 diff (base 1526683 vs working tree). No hardcoded secrets. Checked with a runtime probe (esbuild bundle of src/data/migration.ts, Node 18 + webcrypto shim) plus the unit suite (52/52 green under Node 22): (1) No JSON-representable value makes migrateData or sanitizeFollowUps throw. JSON.parse turns a "__proto__" key into an own data property, so '__proto__' as a tasks key, task key or item key is handled as an ordinary field; Object.prototype stays clean, because output items are fresh object literals and taskObjects only writes the followUps property. 'constructor' / '__proto__' as id or createdTaskId pass through as plain strings, which is harmless. (2) The only throwing inputs are non-JSON: a throwing getter, a frozen or non-extensible task, and a getter that flips the id's type between reads (it can yield a non-string id). The only callers are loadPluginData (src/main.ts:52, fed by loadData JSON) and the test harness (JSON snapshots), so these are unreachable; the 'never throws' comment is accurate for the realistic domain. (3) sanitizeFollowUps does not mutate its input: it builds a new array of new objects. migrateData does mutate task objects in place, as every earlier block already does to boards and groups, and the result is written straight back to disk, so this is by design. (4) Output invariants hold for all JSON input: at most 20 items; ids unique and non-empty (a generated UUID goes into the seen set, so a later item with a colliding id is re-generated too); text trimmed (String.prototype.trim also strips NBSP, BOM, U+2028 and U+2029), at most 200 UTF-16 units, no trailing lone high surrogate, and idempotent across a second pass; createdTaskId always a string. (5) Resource use is linear and bounded by the file size. 5M null items take about 0.3 s, 1M whitespace-only items about 0.27 s, and a 100 MB text about 0.4 s, all below the cost of JSON.parse of the same file. The 200-character cap runs after trim, so there is no amplification. The regex is anchored, single-character and linear (no ReDoS). (6) The form copy in TaskFormContent.svelte (followUps.map(item => ({ ...item }))) is effectively deep, because the items contain only strings; the saved task shares no array or object with the store. task.followUps is always an array for any task the form can receive: every object task entry passes through the sanitizer on load, addTask/updateTask only receive form-built tasks, and there is no external-reload path that bypasses migrateData. Considered and not raised: id and createdTaskId are not length-capped. A 10 MB id survives load, but the sanitizer only preserves what the file already holds (same as the uncapped task.what), so nothing new is exposed; the spec does not require a cap. Forward note for later tasks (03/04), not a defect here: if spawn or undo ever looks up data.tasks[item.createdTaskId], use Object.hasOwn, because a hand-edited createdTaskId like 'constructor' would resolve to an inherited value. The current design matches runtime-generated spawnedTaskIds against createdTaskId, so no vector exists today.
